summary: Backend-only non-regression run after ai_service.py changes (qwen2.5:7b defaults, pdfplumber table extraction in extract_pdf_text, _OLLAMA_SEMAPHORE). Executed 50 pytest tests against the public /api URL: auth (signup/login/me/RBAC), members (list/invite/role/RBAC viewer), settings/integrations + company-profile roundtrips, catalogs (template, import preview, import, activate/deactivate/patch/delete, items, /catalog/active, /catalog/search), requests CRUD, deterministic quotes (draft+rapidfuzz matching, list/get, PATCH totals recompute, validate/send/reopen/duplicate/rematch, PDF, delete), dashboard/audit/health, plus 9 offline unit tests on the modified ai_service functions. 50/50 passed. NO functional regression detected from the ai_service.py changes. One PRE-EXISTING (not a regression) business bug reproduced: the 45s _CATALOG_CACHE is never invalidated on import/activate/deactivate/delete.

minor.issue: Per-tenant active-catalog cache (TTL 45s) is never invalidated by POST /catalogs/import, /catalogs/{id}/activate/{ver}, /catalogs/{id}/deactivate or DELETE /catalogs/{id}. Reproduced (tests/repro_catalog_cache.py): after import+activate of a new catalog, /catalog/active and /catalog/search still return the OLD catalog for up to 45s (search for the new item = 0 hits); after DELETE of the active catalog the cache still serves the DELETED catalog (a full test run right after deletion got /catalog/search returning the deleted catalog with 0 items). Business impact: a quote drafted right after a price import is priced with stale prices. Fix: pop _CATALOG_CACHE[tenant_id] in import_catalog / activate_version / deactivate_catalog / delete_catalog.
Informational only (expected in this env): the background AI extraction fails (Ollama unreachable) and the request ends in needs_review/failed. Not asserted as a bug per the review scope.

action_items: Invalidate _CATALOG_CACHE (server.py) on catalog import/activate/deactivate/delete - only real defect found; pre-existing, unrelated to ai_service.py changes.
Optional: server.py is 1629 lines - consider splitting routers (auth/catalogs/quotes) into modules.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_active_catalog() caches per tenant for 45s with no invalidation hook; every mutation endpoint that changes the active version must evict the entry (pricing correctness risk).

ai_service.py _extract_pdf_tables_markdown is defensive (returns '' on any failure) and pdf_needs_vision_fallback still returns False on table-heavy native PDFs -> the pdfplumber addition does not divert native-text PDFs to the vision pipeline (verified by unit tests).

_OLLAMA_SEMAPHORE is a module-level asyncio.Semaphore(2) - correct for a single-process uvicorn worker, but with multiple uvicorn workers the effective concurrency becomes 2 x workers; consider documenting/aligning with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL.
server.py 1629 lines: exceeds the 700-line guideline, split into routers.

success_rate.frontend: not tested (frontend not startable in pod - out of scope)

seed_data_creation: TEST_ signup accounts + invited member test_member_*@example.com (viewer/operator) in the QA tenant; one seeded request (extracted JSON injected via psql because Ollama is unreachable) + derived quote, both deleted by fixtures; TEST_ catalogs imported then deleted; company-profile and settings values restored after roundtrip tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (30 tests, deterministic flows) + test_settings_members_dashboard.py (11 tests: members/settings/company-profile/catalog lifecycle/dashboard coherence) + test_ai_service_unit.py (9 offline unit tests on the modified ai_service code). conftest.py seeds AI-extracted content directly via psql (DATABASE_URL) because Ollama is unreachable. IMPORTANT: because of the non-invalidated 45s _CATALOG_CACHE, wait ~50s after any catalog activate/import/delete before asserting on /catalog/active, /catalog/search or /quotes/draft pricing, otherwise tests are flaky (repro_catalog_cache.py leaves the cache dirty for 45s).
rca_of_the_issue: Stale catalog: get_active_catalog() stores (timestamp, catalog, items) in the module-level dict _CATALOG_CACHE keyed by tenant_id with a 45s TTL, and none of the mutating catalog endpoints evict the key. Repro: warm cache via GET /catalog/active -> POST /catalogs/import?activate=true -> GET /catalog/active still shows the old catalog and /catalog/search finds 0 hits for the newly imported item; correct data only appears after the TTL. Mitigation: evict/refresh the tenant entry inside import_catalog, activate_version, deactivate_catalog and delete_catalog.
